51193243.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Keap1 kelch domain (unknown origin) by competitive SPR assay
51193243.references_previous: 21. Chen, Y.; Inoyama, D.; Kong, A.-N. T.; Beamer, L. J.; Hu, L. Chem. Biol. Drug Des. 2011, 1014, 78.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The binding constant (Kd) of hit 1 to Keap1 Kelch domain was confirmed to be 1.9 μM (Fig. 2C) using an SPR solution competition assay we recently developed.21
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. (A) The structure of hit 1 identified through HTS, (B) dose–response curve of the hit 1 in the confirmative FP assay, (C) sensorgrams of the hit 1 in the SPR assay, (D) comparison of Kd of different stereoisomers of 5 (LH601) to hit 1, and (E) X-ray crystal structures of A/B as a pair and D as a single enantiomer.
original_paragraph.Figure 2C description: The sensorgrams in Figure 2C show the response units (RU) over time for different concentrations of hit 1. The x-axis represents time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 250 s. The y-axis represents RU, ranging from -20 to 200. The curves show association and dissociation phases, with different concentrations of hit 1 (labeled as 10, 40, 70, 100, 130, 160, 190, 220, 250 nM) producing different response levels. The text states the Kd is 1.9 μM.
